audit.whatIsWrong: Four of the seven rows disagree between layers. The content chart and packet levelChart read Rumble / Skill / Rumble / Rumble / Camille / Rumble / Rumble; CHAMP_FULL.phases reads Skill / Rumble / Rumble / Skill / Skill / Rumble / Rumble. Level 6 is the important one: the chart correctly gives it to Camille because The Hextech Ultimatum arrives, and the full layer calls it Skill.
audit.why: The content whys argue the chart correctly from the kit — Rumble owns 1 and 3-5 on Flamespitter and double Harpoon, Camille takes 6 on her cage. The full layer's rows are unmodified template. EVEN at 6/10 with a 9/10 carry threat is a fair overall read of 52.51%, so the difficulty ratings stand.
audit.corrected: None of the four side values can be changed — Skill to Rumble, Rumble to Skill, Skill to Camille are all outside the plus-or-minus 10 percent band. Recorded in notes for a manual pass.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike says The Hextech Ultimatum 'removes your escape' without giving the cooldown, so the reader has no idea how long the threat lasts or how much a baited R is worth.
audit.why: It is 140/115/90. A 140-second cooldown at rank 1 is two and a half minutes of free lane every time she misses or wastes it, which completely changes how Rumble plays the level 6 window. The other spikes are well placed: Rumble's 4-5 Danger Zone chain and first-item timing are real and correctly described.
audit.corrected: The 140-second rank-1 cooldown written into the level 6 spike and into whys[4].

audit.whatIsWrong: Three gaps. (a) Adaptive Defenses is never mentioned in either layer. It is the single most important interaction in this matchup: her basic attacks on a champion grant her a shield, as a percentage of her maximum health, specifically against that champion's damage type. Rumble is a magic-damage champion, so every auto Camille lands on him buys her a magic shield sized against exactly the damage he is about to deal. A Rumble player who does not know this cannot understand why his trades come up short. (b) Hookshot's terrain requirement is only implied by a stray 'Fight near walls' Don't whose description is mismatched boilerplate about spending a cooldown. She pulls herself to a wall — in the open middle of the lane she has no engage. (c) Tactical Sweep's split is stated as a generic 'W heal' when the mechanic is positional: only enemies in the outer half are slowed, take extra damage and heal her. Standing inside the inner half denies the slow, the bonus damage and the heal at once — and Rumble wants to be close anyway.
audit.why: All three come straight from Riot's descriptions. The Tactical Sweep one is worth more than a generic anti-heal note because it is free: Rumble's Flamespitter is a 600-range cone, so hugging her is already his preferred spacing, and doing it turns her sustain off. The Adaptive Defenses omission explains the whole trade pattern.
audit.corrected: Adaptive Defenses added to the Key Ability Interactions row, the Don'ts, and Camille's wants. Hookshot's wall requirement written into the cooldown breakdown, the Do and the wall Don't. Tactical Sweep's inner-half rule written into the TL;DR, the win condition and Rumble's wants.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hookshot is named as the matchup-defining cooldown eleven times with no number attached, and the text tells the reader to 'E-slow it', which does not describe what Electro Harpoon does to a dash already in flight.
audit.why: Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12, Tactical Sweep 15/14/13/12/11, Precision Protocol 9/8/7/6/5, The Hextech Ultimatum 140/115/90. The genuinely punishable one is Hookshot at 16 seconds, and the better answer than slowing it is denying it a wall.
audit.corrected: Real numbers in the cooldown breakdown; the advice reframed from slowing the dash to fighting where she has no terrain to hook.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] tells the reader Camille wants to 'hit the outer ring of Precision Protocol Q twice'. The outer ring belongs to Tactical Sweep (W); Precision Protocol has no ring.
audit.why: Precision Protocol's real mechanic is the recast: it does significantly increased bonus damage if she delays between the two attacks. That delay is the tell a Rumble player should be reading, and it is being described as something else entirely.

notes: Adaptive Defenses being absent from both layers is the biggest single miss in this matchup and probably in the slice. A percentage-max-health shield that specifically counters the damage type you deal, refreshed off every basic attack she lands on you, is the reason Rumble's trades against Camille feel worse than the numbers suggest. Worth checking whether other AP-versus-Camille matchups have the same hole. Two things I could not fix: four of the seven phases[].side values disagree with the level chart (Skill/Rumble/Rumble/Skill/Skill/Rumble/Rumble against Rumble/Skill/Rumble/Rumble/Camille/Rumble/Rumble) and every one of those swaps breaks the length band; and the full layer refers to Camille as 'he' and 'his' in eight strings, including breakdown.late's 'his healing fights your pattern'. The anti-heal advice itself is correct here — Tactical Sweep genuinely heals her per Riot's text — so I left the itemization row alone apart from noting the pronouns. suspectNames flagged 'Hextech Ultimatum', 'Use Equalizer' and 'Your Equalizer' — all three are false positives, just shortened forms of the real names.
